added_sources.title: Osvaldo Raggio, Microstoria e microstorie (Treccani, 2013)
added_sources.note: Read historical account through the microhistory laboratories section, especially the collective issues of 1976–1987. Participant scholarship; later book-series activity is distinguished from journal publication.

added_sources.title: Oladipupo Olugbodi and Olufunke Adeboye, Decolonization and Functionality of Knowledge in JHSN, 1956–1980 (2025), 19–48
added_sources.note: Downloaded published PDF; read historical development pp. 25–29 and conclusion pp. 41–43, plus abstract. The authors’ evaluation of practical relevance is attributed. Post-1980 continuity is not inferred; the conclusion records revival in 2005.

added_sources.title: JSTOR: Journal of the Historical Society of Nigeria
added_sources.note: Publisher-supplied title, society, 1956 start and ISSN checked. Archive endpoint 2021 is coverage, not cessation.

added_sources.title: Grace E. Riehm et al., What Is Ethnohistory? A Sixty-Year Retrospective (2019), 146–162
added_sources.note: University-hosted scholarly abstract read, not the full article. It reports sampled ten-year intervals from 1954 to 2013, North American predominance and expanding regional/methodological scope. No unreported quantitative results adopted.

added_sources.title: American Society for Ethnohistory: institutional history
added_sources.note: Read society history: Indian Claims Act research, changing institutional identity and journal publication since 1954. Present membership counts are not historical importance measures.

added_sources.title: Roberto Ceamanos Llorens, La historia obrera y social contemporánea en Francia a través del estudio de Le Mouvement Social (1960–2000), ACHSC 33 (2006), 311–336
added_sources.note: Published PDF read: abstract/introduction and conclusions pp. 334–335. Reconstructs the move from organized labour to broader social history. Its developmental judgment about overcoming Marxism is the author’s, not a claim adopted by the atlas.

added_sources.title: Pero Gaglo Dagbovie, Building upon a Century-Long Tradition of Excellence (2019)
added_sources.note: Read editorial retrospective, especially founding, segregation-era role and successive editors through 2001. Post-2002 topic percentages and current circulation are excluded from the pre-2000 selection.

added_sources.title: Annales / Cambridge University Press: Chronology of the journal
added_sources.note: Publisher’s explicit chronology read: 1929–1938, 1939–1941, 1942–1944, 1945, 1946–1993 and 1994 onward. These are title phases, not six unrelated journal foundations.

added_sources.title: Persée: Annales collection and title periods
added_sources.note: Checked post-1938 title identifiers and ESC/HSS boundaries. ESC and HSS share ISSN 0395-2649. The erroneous summary row naming 1929–1937 Mélanges is not adopted; publisher chronology governs. Holdings gaps are not missing publication years.

added_sources.title: Christoph Conrad, Une tradition d’innovation: Les Annales dans le paysage transnational des revues d’histoire, 1990–2020, Annales 75(3–4), 635–648 (2020 issue, online 2021)
added_sources.note: Published repository PDF read pp. 635–642, including scope/method, 1988–1994 transition and thematic examples. Exploratory comparison, not a representative global census. Later issue examples are not backdated.

added_sources.title: Peter Burke: Annales in its wider historical setting
added_sources.note: Reused scoped atlas check: Selected passages checked on generations, Berr, Pirenne, Simiand, and precedents. Comparative parallels are not automatically lines of transmission.

added_sources.title: Annales editors, “Histoire et sciences sociales. Un tournant critique?” (1988), “Tentons l’expérience” (1989); Bernard Lepetit, “L’histoire et les modèles” (1988), collected in the journal’s editorial archive.
added_sources.note: Reused scoped atlas check: Primary 1988 critical-turn text, Annales 43/2:291–293, read, including explicit microhistory/scale discussion; selected opening and closing 1989 passages, 44/6:1317–1323, and selected Lepetit model passages, 43/1:3–4, read. Experiments, evidence, comparison and generalization are discussed without declaring one replacement paradigm. Remaining archive, including the 1996 Lepetit obituary, not reviewed. The later collection date does not extend mapped coverage.

added_sources.title: Sergio Sismondo, 2012 Changes, part II, Social Studies of Science 42(5), 635–637
added_sources.note: Search-indexed opening retrospective read from the Citeseer-hosted published PDF: editorial succession and established STS role by the late 1970s. Direct Sage access unavailable and Citeseer download now 404. Complete editorial not read.

added_sources.title: JSTOR: Social Studies of Science title history
added_sources.note: Title history checked: Science Studies 1971–1974; Social Studies of Science from 1975. 2022 is archive coverage, not cessation.

added_sources.title: Trevor J. Pinch and Wiebe E. Bijker, “The Social Construction of Facts and Artefacts,” Social Studies of Science 14 (1984): 399–441.
added_sources.note: Reused scoped atlas check: Scanned journal pp. 399 and 402 visually inspected: authors explicitly combine SSK and technology research. Abstract names interpretative flexibility, closure and relevant groups; not a full-paper review.

added_sources.title: Robert Nye, Regard sur vingt ans de travaux: le Journal of the History of Sexuality, Clio 31 (2010), 239–266
added_sources.note: Read indexed opening of the article PDF and indexed journal abstract in issue abstracts (clio/pdf/9566), also matching author bibliography. Direct OpenEdition blocked by bot check; Cairn returned 403. Full article unread.

added_edges.relationship: A collective research forum for Italian microhistory.
added_edges.evidence_note: Raggio reconstructs collaborative editorial practice through issues on family/community (1976), villages (1981), local conflict (1986) and land markets (1987).
added_edges.selection_note: Selected for the Italian microhistory strand; it does not represent every form of microhistory or German Alltagsgeschichte. The journal predated this programme.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. Later importance is not assessed by this endpoint.

added_edges.relationship: A society forum for the development of African historical scholarship in Nigeria.
added_edges.evidence_note: The study follows changing methods and historical contributions across the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected for the Nigerian scholarly community and African agency. Nigeria increasingly predominates; the study also identifies limited women’s-history coverage.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. Later importance is not assessed by this endpoint.

added_edges.relationship: A sustained forum for decolonizing accounts of Africa’s past.
added_edges.evidence_note: The retrospective traces challenges to colonial narratives and methodological change across the reviewed period.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected for a Nigerian anti-colonial historiographical strand, not all liberation theories or all African scholarship. Nationalist interpretation and economic relevance remain contested.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. Later importance is not assessed by this endpoint.

added_edges.relationship: An enduring interdisciplinary venue for historical research on Indigenous peoples, especially in the Americas.
added_edges.evidence_note: The society history and longitudinal abstract establish continuing publication and changing research scope.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected as an ethnohistorical interlocutor within this broad entry. Publication about Indigenous peoples does not establish Indigenous control of research or endorsement of decolonizing methods.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. 2000 is the atlas coverage boundary.

added_edges.relationship: A sustained French venue for labour history and an expanding social history.
added_edges.evidence_note: Ceamanos traces four decades of institutionalization and changes in questions, communities and methods.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected for the French labour/social-history community. The predecessor L’Actualité de l’Histoire is not backdated under this title; no exclusive Marxist affiliation is inferred.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. 2000 is the atlas coverage boundary.

added_edges.relationship: A continuing institutional and scholarly home for African American history.
added_edges.evidence_note: Dagbovie traces the journal’s role across successive editorial generations, beyond Woodson’s initial programme.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected for sustained African American historical scholarship. The original title applies throughout this interval; the 2002 renaming does not truncate the field’s history.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. 2000 is the atlas coverage boundary.

added_edges.relationship: The early journal forum associated with the Annales movement.
added_edges.evidence_note: Burke’s previously checked generational history supports this early phase; publisher chronology bounds the original title.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected for the movement’s early journal community. This supplements the founding edge; it does not imply a uniform doctrine or erase antecedents.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. Later importance is not assessed by this endpoint.

added_edges.relationship: A sustained postwar journal forum for successive Annales approaches.
added_edges.evidence_note: The generational history, 1988–1989 editorial reconsideration and Conrad’s transition analysis support the postwar interval.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected across changing programmes, not as one unchanging school. The ESC title ends in 1993; the publication continues.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. Later importance is not assessed by this endpoint.

added_edges.relationship: A continuing Annales forum for historical inquiry in dialogue with the social sciences.
added_edges.evidence_note: Conrad studies the 1990s editorial transition and recurring thematic work; publisher chronology identifies the 1994 subtitle change.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected for the journal community’s continued, self-critical development. Its refusal of doctrinal closure is retained; this is not an extension of Braudel’s programme unchanged.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. 2000 is the atlas coverage boundary.

added_edges.relationship: An established interdisciplinary forum for science and technology studies.
added_edges.evidence_note: Sismondo’s retrospective identifies an established field role by the late 1970s and editorial continuity through 2002; the 1984 Pinch–Bijker contribution anchors the technology interface.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected from 1980, after the documented late-1970s consolidation. Evidence includes a limited indexed retrospective; STS is broader than SSK and no exclusive school allegiance is assigned.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. 2000 is the atlas coverage boundary.

added_edges.relationship: A specialist forum for historical studies of sexuality during the 1990s.
added_edges.evidence_note: Nye’s twenty-year retrospective abstract reviews changing questions, periods and methods, particularly women’s sexuality; the opening identifies the 1990 launch.
added_edges.selection_note: Selected for sexuality history within the combined sexuality/queer entry, not as a journal uniformly committed to queer theory. Full-text review remains a follow-up.

temporal_scope.note: Evidenced selection interval, not a field lifespan or a claim of journal cessation. 2000 is the atlas coverage boundary.
